The Evidence Room

Child Custody & Shared Parenting Judgments

Rulings on custody, visitation and parenting time, shared parenting, parental alienation, and a child’s right to a relationship with both parents.

43 judgments · 19 from the Supreme Court · updated 25 November 2026

In Indian custody cases the deciding test is the welfare of the child, not the rights of either parent. Courts have increasingly said that welfare usually means keeping both parents meaningfully involved: a parent ‘cannot be a guest in a child’s life’, and acrimony between the parents is not by itself a reason to deny access.

This page collects rulings on custody and visitation, shared-parenting and parenting-time guidelines, parental alienation, habeas corpus for children, relocation abroad, and enforcement of visitation orders, including contempt for breaching them.

Co-Parenting Karnataka High Court
Mother v. Father (parties not named in report)
November 2026

Dismissed a mother’s writ petition against a Family Court order giving the father overnight parenting time on the first and third weekends of each month, holding that the child’s welfare cannot be invoked as a ‘convenient justification’ for disregarding a custody order.

Babita v. Pramod (2026 SCC OnLine Del 8314)
October 2026

Division Bench dismissed the mother’s appeal and upheld the father’s regular visitation with his 15-year-old son, holding that a child’s contact with a parent can be cut off only in exceptional circumstances, for reasons the court records.

A v. B (2026 INSC 818)
August 2026

Custody of a minor awarded to maternal grandparents under parens patriae jurisdiction after the Court personally interviewed the child. Father directed to rebuild the child’s confidence before supervised visitation resumes.

Co-Parenting Delhi High Court
Neha Relhan v. Deepak Relhan
August 2026

Division Bench dismissed the mother’s appeal against a Family Court order directing police to hand the child to the father. The 2025 interim custody order continues to operate, and pending recall or review applications cannot stall its enforcement.

Co-Parenting Delhi High Court
Disha Gupta v. Gaurav Batra — Overnight Custody Not Warranted Where Child Had Never Stayed With Father
June 19, 2026

Set aside a Family Court order granting overnight custody for being inconsistent with its own finding that the child had never stayed overnight with the father and needed time to adjust. Substituted extended daytime custody (9 AM–8 PM) as a graduated step rather than denying access outright.

Co-Parenting Supreme Court
Sheetal Vasant Thakur v. Chirag Arora (2026 INSC 638)
June 2026

Psychological evaluation of a child cannot be ordered routinely in custody or visitation disputes. 20 detailed observations issued: minimum intrusion must be the norm, single neutral expert, child’s welfare is paramount. Repeated evaluations risk re-traumatisation.

Co-Parenting Kerala High Court
Hayarunisa Abdul Hakkim v. Director General of Police & Ors.
June 2026

Directed all Family Courts in Kerala to follow the Calcutta High Court’s Child Access & Custody Guidelines until state-specific rules are framed, restoring a child’s custody to the mother after the father unlawfully removed her from school in violation of a standing decree. Shows the Calcutta framework already on this list spreading as binding practice across states.

LANDMARK Read Full Judgment →
Co-Parenting Delhi High Court
Somya Goel v. State (NCT of Delhi) & Anr.
June 2026

Complex custody disputes involving competing allegations, foreign court proceedings, and disputed facts about a child’s welfare belong before the competent Family Court, not a summary habeas corpus writ. Mother’s habeas petition over her autistic daughter dismissed — chiefly because she concealed related Singapore court proceedings — and relegated to pending Family Court proceedings.

Co-Parenting Supreme Court
Hamsaanandini Nanduri v. Union of India (2026 INSC 246)
March 2026

Supreme Court read down Section 60(4) of the Code on Social Security, 2020, holding its 3-month age limit unconstitutional for denying maternity benefits to adoptive mothers. The bench also separately urged Parliament to legislate paternity leave — ‘proximity is not identical to presence.’

Poonam Wadhwa v. Ajay Wadhwa (SLP(Crl) No. 12458/2024)
November 25, 2025

Work-from-home status and minor differences in distance to school cannot be decisive factors in child custody. Supreme Court upheld custody to the father, rejecting the mother’s plea based on a flexible work arrangement.

Co-Parenting Calcutta High Court
Calcutta HC Child Access & Custody Guidelines
Sept 2025

Landmark shared parenting framework — both parents presumed equal. Guaranteed weekend overnight visits, holidays, festivals. Courts told to stay vigilant against parental alienation.

Co-Parenting Supreme Court
Manoj Dhankar v. Neeharika & Ors. (2025 INSC 1068)
August 25, 2025

A mother relocating a child abroad cannot cut off the father’s relationship with the child. Supreme Court formally recognised video-conferencing as a valid, enforceable mode of parental visitation in cross-border custody disputes.

Co-Parenting Delhi High Court
Vimlendu Kumar Jha v. Minal Bhatnagar
May 30, 2025

Father’s role is equally vital for a child’s emotional and psychological development. Visitation rights are not dependent on the custodial parent’s consent — guided solely by the child’s best interests. No rigid formula including 50% vacation division can be applied in custody matters.

In a dispute between parents over their 22-year-old son with cerebral palsy, the Supreme Court relied on an expert (NIMHANS) assessment of his capacity and directed that he live with his mother and brother in Bengaluru, with daily visits for the father.

Co-Parenting Supreme Court
Vivek Kumar Chaturvedi v. State of UP (2025 INSC 159)
Feb 2025

Father’s remarriage cannot be a ground to deny child custody. Grandparents have no superior claim over the natural guardian. Father’s legal right as natural guardian must be respected in the absence of any adverse conduct against him.

Co-Parenting P&H High Court
Navjot Kaur v. State of Punjab & Ors
July 11, 2024

Father and mother are two sides of the same coin — a family is incomplete without synergies of both parents. Court ordered 50/50 holiday custody, structured weekend visitation (Friday 5PM to Sunday 5PM), joint celebration of birthdays and festivals, and recurring deposit by father for children’s education. Passports require consent of both parents. (CRWP-5895-2023)

Using these judgments

Official Court Copy opens the judgment PDF from the Supreme Court’s own website. Full Judgment opens the complete judgment text (Indian Kanoon, or a PDF copy of the order). Read Report opens a news or legal-blog summary where no full text is linked yet.

To rely on a judgment in court, cite it by its case number or citation; the court’s registry can issue a certified copy. Check that it has not been overturned or modified on appeal. The one-line summaries on this page are for information only and are not legal advice.
